title: List toolbar: offer the "In a queue" toggle only when the organization has at least one queue — today every owned object shows it, and in an app with no queues it always returns an empty list
body:
epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

Filed by the record-page epic seat (part of the record and list review under #26676) after the maintainer asked, on the latest main, 「右侧显示的 在队列中是什么，每个业务对象都需要显示吗」 and answered the seat's recommendation with 「立卡」 (2026-10-31).

## Reading (origin/main `5da3a8ce31`)

- The list toolbar's **In a queue** toggle (`list.sittingInQueue`, zh 「在队列中」, hint "Show only records waiting in a queue for someone to claim them") came with the ownership-queue work (ADR-0142, #27264). When it is on, the list adds `owner_id is_empty` AND `queue is_not_empty` (`QUEUE_SITTING_CONDITIONS`, `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` around line 864).
- It is offered whenever `objectHasOwnershipQueue(objectDef)` is true (`ListView.tsx` line 878, read at line 2147, rendered at line 5707). That check asks only whether the served definition carries the platform-injected system field `queue`.
- ADR-0142 D3 injects `queue` on every object that gets `owner_id`, which means every `ownership: 'user'` object. `'user'` is the default. So the toggle sits on practically every business list, whether or not the deployment has a single queue.
- In both apps the seat previews, it is a control that can never return a row. HotCRM declares no queue: none of its 18 objects overrides the default, so all 18 lists show the toggle. `examples/app-crm` declares none either. Neither app has a `sys_queue` row or an assignment rule that would route a record into a queue.

## Target

Offer the toggle only when the current organization resolves **at least one queue**. Use the same two sources ADR-0142 D6 defines and the console's queue picker already reads: declared queues plus the organization's `sys_queue` rows (`useTwoSourceCandidates` / `mergeQueueCandidates`, used by `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowReferenceField.tsx`). With no queue at all, the toggle is not rendered.

- Keep the injected `queue` column and everything the server does with it (claim, release, the read rule). This card narrows only when the toolbar offers the filter. No spec or contract change.
- Read the queue set once per session or organization and reuse it across lists, so list mounts add no request.
- Keep the record page's Claim affordance (`useQueueClaimOffered`, `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/queueClaim.ts`) as it is. It already asks the server per record.

### Premise to verify first

An ordinary end user, not only an admin, can read both sources: the declared-queue registry and `sys_queue` rows, or an equivalent served list of queue names.

- If not, stop and report it as a fork in `out_of_scope_findings`.
- Do not fall back to showing the toggle everywhere, and do not hide it everywhere.
- The seat will decide whether the record page payload or the session should carry an "organization has queues" bit.

Do not narrow per object (offer the filter only where a queue or an assignment rule targets this object) on this card. That needs a server reading the console does not get today. File it as a follow-up finding if the dev sees real pull for it.

## Why (four axes)

- **Business need:** in a deployment without queues, the toggle has no scenario. Both real apps the seat reads are such deployments. Where queues exist, nothing changes.
- **Long-term fit:** a control that can only return an empty list is the same class of defect as #27831, which stopped the list header from offering single-record actions when no row can be selected. The rule is the same: offer an affordance only when it can do something.
- **AI-error resistance:** an AI that writes an app gets no queue UI it did not ask for. The gate reads data the app declares, not a new key.
- **Startup focus:** this removes an affordance and adds no surface: no new key, no new gate.

## Acceptance

1. On HotCRM and `examples/app-crm` on main, no list shows **In a queue**.
2. Declare one queue, or insert one `sys_queue` row. The toggle appears on owned objects' lists, and turning it on filters exactly as it does today.
3. The existing tests in `ListView.queueSittingFilter-25769.test.tsx` still pass. New tests pin the no-queue case (toggle absent) and the one-queue case (toggle present).
4. Opening a list adds no request; the network count is the same before and after.
